item.title: Dangerous parking, 31st July
item.description:
Dear team I am writing to raise a road safety concern regarding the T-junction of Guinevere Road and Tennyson Road. Visibility when exiting Guinevere Road is extremely poor because vehicles are parked on the pavement and on Tennyson Road directly opposite the junction. This makes it very difficult to see oncoming traffic and creates a dangerous situation for all road users. The situation is especially hazardous in the mornings when children are cycling to school. I have personally experienced two near misses, one involving an e-scooter rider, and another involving a young boy on a bicycle. Children travelling to school are often difficult to see when pulling out of Guinevere Road, which significantly increases the risk of a serious accident. I have reported this issue to the police twice. On both occasions, I was advised to contact the local council, as they agreed that the junction presents a safety risk. I believe that double yellow lines should be installed around this T-junction to prevent parking too close to the junction and improve visibility. This would greatly reduce the risk of a future accident. There are 33 houses on Guinevere Road, and many households own two cars. Almost all residents use this junction when leaving for work each morning, so this affects a large number of people every day. I would be grateful if the council could investigate this matter and consider taking action. I hope that any necessary improvements could be made during the school holidays so that the junction is safer when children return to school in the autumn.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 28, Tennyson Road, Hatherley, Cheltenham, Cheltenham

item.title: The tree is in desperate need of pruning, 31st July
item.description:
It is ion the adopted Highway I am writing to request that the council considers inspecting and, if appropriate, pruning the tree situated outside my mother's property. Over time, the tree has become significantly overgrown, with branches now extending well over the boundary into my mother's front garden. As the tree has matured, it has also begun to block a considerable amount of natural light from entering her front room, leaving it noticeably darker throughout the day. Whilst I appreciate that trees provide many benefits and that maintenance has to be carefully managed, the current situation is having a real impact on my mother. She is elderly and spends a great deal of time at home. The lack of natural light, together with the overhanging branches, has become a constant source of worry for her. She has become increasingly anxious about the tree and has become quite fixated on it, which is affecting her wellbeing and enjoyment of her home. I would therefore be very grateful if the council could arrange for an inspection to assess whether the tree would benefit from pruning. I am not requesting that the tree be removed, only that it is appropriately maintained so that it no longer overhangs the property to the same extent and allows more natural light into her home. 66 Cleevemount Road Cheltenham Glos GL52 3HE
